text:
sanjay: quick favor — ran a 2h prod-sim workload and noticed a ~6% drop in KV prefix cache hit-rate on shard-7 around 11:18. can someone try to reproduce with key sampling? cc @claire @toni
claire: on it. do you have the exact window and the load profile you used?
sanjay: window 11:10–11:25, step load: bursty small-ctx chats (avg seq len 120). i pushed the run config to /perf/runs/1795, name=kv-frag-check.
toni: i can spin up a quick nightly replay against the canary cluster. expect ~30m to setup. want me to enable prefix sampling (1:1000) or full debug?
sanjay: start with 1:1000 sampling + record eviction events only. if that looks noisy, switch to 1:100.
alex: heads-up, perf-bot just flagged a related spike in eviction churn earlier this morning:
perf-bot: [ALERT] eviction_churn_rate > threshold on shard-7 (11:14:22) — suspect workload pattern change. See /alerts/evict-1795
claire: i'll run the replay with sampling and upload a small aggregated CSV of key prefixes + hit_count + eviction_ts. if we see hot-prefix fragmentation we should correlate with model switch events.
toni: running now. command i'm using:
```bash
./tools/replay --run /perf/runs/1795 --target canary --sample-prefix 1000 --evict-log /tmp/evict-1795.log
```
sanjay: perfect. also pls dump kv-occupancy histogram for the shard: `/admin/kv-stats --shard 7 --histogram`
claire: got a quick question — when we sample 1:1000, do we still log TTL and last-access node? want to ensure we can map to request traces.
alex: sampling includes last_access_node but not full request trace by default. to attach traces set `--trace-sample 1:10000` (very low).
toni: replay finished — uploading a 6MB artifact to S3: s3://redwood-perf/kv/1795123456/evict-sample.csv
sanjay: thanks. can you paste the top 10 prefixes by eviction count?
toni: top 10 prefixes (prefix, evict_count):
1) "usr:profile:photo"  134
2) "chat:session:ctx"    98
3) "embed:recent"        86
4) "model:token-cache"   72
5) "usr:settings"        41
6) "bot:ctx:temp"        39
7) "doc:page:render"     33
8) "session:stream"      28
9) "search:term"         21
10) "analytics:meta"     19
claire: interesting — "model:token-cache" spikes line up with a canary model swap at 11:13. that could explain increased churn for long-tail prefixes.
sanjay: ok — hypothesis: new model has slightly different tokenization leading to prefix mismatch and more distinct keys, increasing fragmentation -> lower hit-rate. action items: 1) add a temporary prefix coalescing rule for model:token-cache to reduce cardinality, 2) re-run perf with that rule, 3) if helps, include in rollback playbook.
alex: i can throw together the coalescing rule as a small config patch. propose: collapse last two tokens for that namespace. patch will be a config flag, e.g., `coalesce_suffix_tokens=2` for prefix="model:token-cache".
toni: ran with coalescing flag in canary; hit-rate improved ~3.5% in 20m window and eviction churn dropped ~28%.
claire: uploading results to the run artifact: s3://redwood-perf/kv/1795123456/coalesce-results.json
sanjay: great. can someone open a short PR with the rule and add a one-line note in the rollout playbook about the tokenization fragility? tagging @alex for the PR and @claire for the playbook change.
alex: will open PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9421 — title: "kv: coalesce model:token-cache suffix tokens to reduce fragmentation"
claire: i added the playbook note in docs/rollouts/kv-fragmentation.md in the PR comments.
sanjay: thanks all. filing a quick follow-up for later: monitor next 24h and if any other shards show similar behavior, escalate to model oncall. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: [NOTE] monitoring alert created: MON-1795123456 (24h watch on shard-7)
